reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Principal office location at state capital
headings.reviewNote: Principal office of commission located at Jefferson City and provided by board of public buildings.

headings.title: Continuous session and full-time commissioner duty
headings.reviewNote: Commission open and in session for business on all days except Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays; commissioners devote entire time to office.

headings.title: Official seal and judicial notice
headings.reviewNote: Official seal inscribed 'Public Service Commission of the State of Missouri' affixed to writs/authentications and judicially noticed by all courts.

headings.title: Commission litigation capacity and office supplies
headings.reviewNote: Commission may sue and be sued in official name; office supplied with necessary books, maps, furniture, connections, appliances, and incidentals.

headings.title: Business office hours and continuous designated staff
headings.reviewNote: Offices open during business hours except Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays with one or more designated responsible persons on duty.

headings.title: Service of process on secretary or commissioner
headings.reviewNote: State or federal court summons or writ served on secretary or any commissioner at Jefferson City office constitutes service on entire commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-2009 history notes; all 6 headings retained; note catchline retains 'commissioners to reside where' though residency text is absent from the body.

headings.title: Independent technical advisory staff retention
headings.reviewNote: Commission may retain independent technical advisory staff of up to six full-time employees in specified fields.

headings.title: Commissioner personal advisors
headings.reviewNote: Each commissioner may retain one personal advisor serving at commissioner pleasure with technical expertise.

headings.title: Cost-neutral staffing offset requirement
headings.reviewNote: Technical advisory staff and personal advisors established only with corresponding elimination in comparable staff positions.

headings.title: Advisory duties and privileged communications
headings.reviewNote: Advisors assist commissioners and judges on technical matters; deliberation communications privileged from disclosure.

headings.title: Periodic updates on regulatory developments and trends
headings.reviewNote: Technical advisory staff periodically updates commission and judges on public utility regulation trends.

headings.title: Ex parte and conflict of interest restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Advisors subject to commissioner ex parte rules; prior employees of regulated entities recused from prior cases.

headings.title: Prohibition on advisory staff appearing as parties
headings.reviewNote: Technical advisory staff and personal advisors barred from being a party to any case before commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2003-2019 history notes; all 7 headings retained covering permissive retention of technical advisory staff and personal advisors, cost-neutral offset, privileged advice, regulatory updates, ex parte/recusal rules, and bar on party status.

headings.title: Selection and publication of official commission reports
headings.reviewNote: Publications commission selects findings, orders, and decisions for official publication in serially numbered electronic or bound volumes.

headings.title: Advance sheets and evidentiary effect of reports
headings.reviewNote: Publications commission publishes advance sheets of selected decisions; official reports are competent evidence without further proof or authentication.

headings.title: Syllabi, headnotes, indexes, and case digests
headings.reviewNote: Publications commission supervises preparation and publication of syllabi/headnotes, indexes, tables of cases, and digests.

headings.title: Other utility regulation publications and sale pricing
headings.reviewNote: Publications commission selects and publishes other utility-regulation works or studies in pamphlet, book, or electronic form and sells publications at approximate printing cost.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1947/2013 history notes; replaced hallucinated headings in subsections 2-4 and refined subsection 1 to match official reports, advance sheets as competent evidence, syllabi/digests, and other publications for sale.

headings.title: Annual compensation of publications commission members
headings.reviewNote: Each member receives $52,000 annually in equal monthly installments, paid half from the Public Service Commission Fund (386.370) and half from the state highway department fund; Revisor's Note cites Appendix E salary adjustment index under 105.005.

headings.title: Annual reports to governor on federal regulatory actions
headings.reviewNote: Members serving on August 13, 1984 must submit annual reports to the governor on federal actions affecting state regulation under chapters 386 to 393 until their then-current terms expire.

headings.title: Additional compensation for federal-action reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Members performing subsection 2 duties receive additional compensation bringing total pay to the combined compensation under section 386.150 and subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1947-1984 history, and Revisor's Note referencing Appendix E (section 105.005); replaced all 3 hallucinated headings to reflect member compensation, 1984 federal-action reports to the governor, and extra-duty compensation.

headings.title: Prohibited employment solicitation and gifts from utilities
headings.reviewNote: Commissioners, public counsel, and staff prohibited from soliciting utility employment; utilities and personnel prohibited from offering positions, free passes/fares, free carriage, gifts, or gratuities.

headings.title: Removal from office and public officer status
headings.reviewNote: Commissioners, public counsel, or staff violating section are removed from office and are deemed public officers.

headings.title: Civil penalty against violating public utilities
headings.reviewNote: Violating public utility liable in attorney general civil action for up to $20,000 civil penalty, paid to general revenue, in addition to other chapter penalties.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for utility officers and employees
headings.reviewNote: Utility officer, agent, or employee violating section commits a misdemeanor punishable by up to $1,000 fine, up to one year in county jail, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939/1977 history notes; replaced all 4 hallucinated headings to reflect conflict-of-interest/gift prohibitions, removal from office, utility civil penalties up to $20,000, and utility personnel misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Conferences with public, utilities, and other agencies
headings.reviewNote: Commission may confer in person, by correspondence, or at conventions with the public, utilities, or state and federal commissions or agencies on its duties.

headings.title: Communications on matters not in filed cases
headings.reviewNote: Permits communications addressing any issue not currently the subject of a case filed with the commission.

headings.title: Communications in pending cases without scheduled hearings
headings.reviewNote: Allows substantive or procedural communications in pending cases without a scheduled evidentiary hearing at posted agenda meetings, all-party forums, or with next-business-day written/oral disclosure filing and service.

headings.title: Free exchange on general regulatory policy
headings.reviewNote: Preserves free exchange of ideas and information on general regulatory policy not addressing the merits of a pending case unless complying with subsection 3.

headings.title: Briefings to officials and agenda procedural discussions
headings.reviewNote: Commission or commissioners may advise legislators or officials on pending issues without expressing merits opinions, and discuss procedural matters or unanimous stipulations at public agenda meetings.

headings.title: Cooperative agreements and receipt of financial assistance
headings.reviewNote: Commission may enter cooperative agreements or act as agent/licensee with federal or other state entities and deposit received grants or assistance in the PSC utility fund or state highway commission fund.

headings.title: Joint investigations, hearings, and concurrent orders
headings.reviewNote: Commission may conduct joint investigations and hearings within or outside Missouri and issue joint or concurrent orders with other state or federal commissions or agencies.

headings.title: Intervention in federal, state, and judicial proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Commission may appear, participate, and intervene in federal, state, or other administrative, regulatory, or judicial proceedings pending or commenced after August 28, 2013.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-2013 history notes; replaced hallucinated headings in subsections 2-8 and broadened subsection 1 to match conferences, pending-case communication rules, policy exchanges, official briefings, cooperative agreements/funds, joint hearings, and intervention authority.

headings.title: Electric fuel and purchased-power rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Electrical corporation may apply for interim energy charge or periodic rate adjustments for prudently incurred fuel, purchased-power, and transportation costs, with optional efficiency incentives.

headings.title: Environmental compliance cost rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Electrical, gas, or water corporation may apply for periodic rate adjustments for environmental compliance costs, capped at 2.5% of gross jurisdictional revenues annually (excluding pass-through taxes), with deferral of excess costs.

headings.title: Weather and conservation usage rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Gas or electrical corporation may apply for periodic adjustments for weather/conservation usage impacts on eligible classes; applies to electrical corporations Jan 1, 2019 through Jan 1, 2029 (expiration noted in source footnote), with non-concurrent limit with 393.1400(5) deferrals.

headings.title: Water corporation revenue variation rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Water corporation with over 8,000 Missouri retail customers may apply for periodic rate adjustments to match established revenue requirement across usage variations.

headings.title: Approval standards, true-ups, rate cases, and prudence reviews
headings.reviewNote: Commission may approve, modify, or reject subsection 1-4 mechanisms only after general rate proceeding hearing; requires fair return design, annual true-up with interest, and for subs 1-2 a four-year general rate case and 18-month prudence reviews.

headings.title: Continuation of approved adjustment mechanisms
headings.reviewNote: Approved mechanism remains in effect until commission authorizes modification, extension, or discontinuance in a general rate case or complaint proceeding.

headings.title: Separate disclosure of adjustment charges on customer bills
headings.reviewNote: Amounts charged under any approved adjustment mechanism must be separately disclosed on each customer bill.

headings.title: Consideration of business risk in allowed return
headings.reviewNote: Commission may consider business-risk changes from an adjustment mechanism when setting allowed return in any rate proceeding.

headings.title: Binding effect of approved incentive or performance plans
headings.reviewNote: Lawfully approved incentive- or performance-based plan binds the commission for its entire term; neither authorizes nor prohibits such plans.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and applications without rules
headings.reviewNote: Commission authorized to promulgate chapter 536 rules (prior to Aug 28, 2005 for subs 1-3; upon Aug 28, 2018 for sub 4); utilities may apply regardless of whether rules are promulgated.

headings.title: Existing ratemaking mechanisms unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Section does not affect any existing approved adjustment mechanism, tariff, incentive plan, or ratemaking mechanism.

headings.title: Severability of section provisions
headings.reviewNote: Each provision of the section is severable if any provision or subsection is deemed unlawful.

headings.title: Effective date and prior rulemaking for subsections 1 to 3
headings.reviewNote: Subsections 1 to 3 take effect January 1, 2006; commission must have previously promulgated application-process rules before issuing orders under them.

headings.title: Task force on conservation and weatherization programs
headings.reviewNote: Commission must appoint a task force of interested parties to study and recommend cost recovery and implementation of electric and gas conservation and weatherization programs.

headings.title: Quarterly surveillance monitoring reports and 2029 expiration
headings.reviewNote: Utilities under subsection 3 mechanisms must file quarterly five-part surveillance monitoring reports (rate base, capitalization, income statement, jurisdictional allocation, financial data notes); subsection expires January 1, 2029 (source footnote).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 2005-2022 history, expiration footnotes (Jan 1, 2029 for electric sub 3 and sub 15), and section 393.1675 nonseverability cross-reference; replaced hallucinated headings in subsections 2-15 and tightened subsection 1.

headings.title: Written commission orders, recording, and constructive notice
headings.reviewNote: Orders, authorizations, and certificates must be written and recorded; certified copies and status certificates may be recorded in county/city recorder offices to impart notice.

headings.title: Required in-state utility office and record retention
headings.reviewNote: Every public utility must maintain a Missouri office keeping required accounts, records, books, and papers, which may not be removed from the state except under commission conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 history note; replaced both hallucinated headings to reflect written/recorded commission orders imparting notice and the required in-state utility office for keeping records.

headings.title: Rules establishing fees for copies and electronic transmittals
headings.reviewNote: Commission may adopt rules setting charges for copies of records, orders, certificates, reports, transcripts, and electronic transmittals in compliance with section 610.026, RSMo Supp. 1993.

headings.title: Fee schedule for certificates authorizing debt issues
headings.reviewNote: Tiered fee schedule ($1/$0.50/$0.25 per $1,000, $25 minimum) for certificates authorizing bonds, notes, or debt issues; exempts refunding, guaranteeing, or retiring existing debt.

headings.title: Fee exemptions for public officers and monthly remittance
headings.reviewNote: No copy fees for public officers in official capacity or ordinary annual report distribution; commission may charge for publications; all fees remitted monthly to director of revenue.

headings.title: Deposit and allocation of collected fees
headings.reviewNote: Subsection 1 copy fees deposited to the commission fund paying copy expenses; subsection 2 debt-issue fees deposited in the state's general revenue fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-1995 history notes; replaced all 4 hallucinated subpoena headings to match copy-fee rules (610.026), debt-certificate fee schedule, public-officer exemptions/monthly remittance, and fee fund deposits.

headings.title: Health and safety orders and emergency waivers
headings.reviewNote: Commission may require persons, corporations, municipal gas systems, and public utilities to maintain safe operations, minimize retail electric line duplication for safety, and waive notice/hearing for imminent serious harm with prompt post-order hearing.

headings.title: Prohibition on electric territorial allocation rules or orders
headings.reviewNote: Bars commission from making any rule, regulation, decree, or order allocating territory or territorial rights among electric suppliers under sections 386.310 and 394.160.

headings.title: Gas pipeline safety jurisdiction scope
headings.reviewNote: Extends gas pipeline safety jurisdiction to single-meter distribution systems (excluding petroleum gas), high-pressure pipelines for owner consumption, intrastate facilities of interstate pipelines serving direct-sales customers, and gas plants supplying institutional buildings like schools and hospitals.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-1996 history notes; replaced hallucinated subsection 2 heading and refined subsections 1 and 3 to match health/safety orders and emergency waivers, bar on electric territorial allocation, and gas pipeline safety scope.

headings.title: Protection of collective bargaining terms and FAS 106 expenses
headings.reviewNote: Commission cannot alter collective bargaining employment terms; recognizes actuarially sound FAS 106 retiree benefit expenses.

headings.title: External funding mechanism for postretirement benefit obligations
headings.reviewNote: Utility using FAS 106 must use independent external trust; nonreversion to utility; commission ratemaking authority preserved.

headings.title: Tariff filing for FAS 106 revenue requirement and amortization
headings.reviewNote: Utilities with 1993-1994 rate orders may file one set of tariffs reflecting FAS 106 obligations amortized up to 20 years; commission may suspend up to 150 days and examine only FAS 106/rate design issues.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1993-1994 history notes; all 3 headings retained covering collective bargaining and FAS 106 ratemaking protections, independent nonreverting external funding, and 1993-1994 FAS 106 tariff filing/suspension rules.

headings.title: General supervision of telegraph and telephone corporations
headings.reviewNote: Commission exercises general supervision over telegraph and telephone corporations and lines, examining condition, capitalization, franchises, service adequacy, and legal compliance.

headings.title: Inspection of telegraph and telephone property
headings.reviewNote: Commission members, engineers, inspectors, or employees authorized to enter and inspect property, buildings, plants, offices, apparatus, and lines of covered corporations or persons.

headings.title: Examination and subpoena of books and records
headings.reviewNote: Commission and commissioners may examine books, contracts, records, documents, and papers, compel production by subpoena duces tecum, or require sworn copies.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-1996 history, and cross-references (394.160, Chap. 392); retained subsection 1 and aligned subsections 2-3 with statutory terminology (telegraph/telephone property inspection and book/record examination or sworn copies).

headings.title: Commission investigations of telecommunications companies
headings.reviewNote: Commission may investigate telecommunications company acts/omissions on own motion and shall investigate violations of law or commission orders.

headings.title: Complaints by public counsel or aggrieved persons
headings.reviewNote: Public counsel or aggrieved persons may file complaints; utility given time to satisfy or answer charges.

headings.title: Final commission order within sixty days of submission
headings.reviewNote: Commission must issue order dismissing complaint or directing satisfaction within sixty days of final submission.

headings.title: Jurisdiction limits over yellow pages and telephone cooperatives
headings.reviewNote: Commission lacks jurisdiction over yellow page listing/ad complaints (ratemaking imputation preserved) or telephone cooperative local exchange rates except exchange access service.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-1996 history notes; all 4 headings retained covering own-motion/mandatory investigations, written complaints and reparation/answer procedure, 60-day final order deadline, and yellow-pages and telephone-cooperative jurisdiction exclusions.

headings.title: Mandamus or injunction proceedings against public utilities
headings.reviewNote: General counsel commences circuit court mandamus or injunction actions (including temporary, preliminary, and permanent relief) against utilities, municipal gas systems, persons, or corporations.

headings.title: Answer deadline and summary court inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Court sets answer deadline up to 30 days where contemplated by Missouri Rules of Court and immediately inquires into facts without formal pleadings or technical requirements.

headings.title: Joinder of necessary or proper parties
headings.reviewNote: Court may join other necessary or proper persons, utilities, municipal gas systems, or corporations as parties upon general counsel's application.

headings.title: Final judgment dismissing action or granting relief
headings.reviewNote: Final judgment either dismisses the action or directs issuance of a writ of mandamus, an injunction, or both as prayed or modified.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-1989 history (effective 6-13-89); retained subsection 1 and replaced shifted/hallucinated headings in subsections 2-4 to match answer deadline/summary inquiry, party joinder, and final judgment.

headings.title: Annual expense estimates by public utility group
headings.reviewNote: Commission estimates annual regulatory expenses before each fiscal year starting July 1, 1947, separately by utility group (water and sewer combined) plus unallocated expenses.

headings.title: Allocation of expenses and assessment caps
headings.reviewNote: Allocates direct and proportional unallocated expenses by group and assesses utilities proportionally; caps total assessment at 0.45% of gross intrastate revenues (non-telecom) and 0.25% (telecom including interconnected VoIP).

headings.title: Assessment statements and payment or installment schedule
headings.reviewNote: Commission renders statement by July 1; utilities pay director of revenue in full by July 15 or in four equal installments (July 15, Oct 15, Jan 15, Apr 15); remitted to state treasurer.

headings.title: Public Service Commission Fund and carryover reductions
headings.reviewNote: Treasurer credits payments to Public Service Commission Fund (or successor under repealed section 33.571*); unexpended balances do not revert and reduce next year's assessments proportionally.

headings.title: Annual sworn revenue statements and binding commission estimates
headings.reviewNote: Utilities must file sworn gross intrastate operating revenue statements by March 31 annually (and within 10 days of Aug 28, 1996); commission makes binding estimate upon failure to file.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-2025 history, and footnote noting repeal of section 33.571 (H.B. 1965, 2010); fixed shifted headings across subsections 1-5 covering expense estimates, group allocation and 0.45%/0.25% caps, billing/installments, PSC Fund carryovers, and annual revenue statements.

headings.title: Public records and annual report to governor
headings.reviewNote: All commission proceedings, documents, and records are public records; annual report of preceding fiscal year submitted to governor by second Monday in January and laid before legislature.

headings.title: Hearings on pending legislation and legislative recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Commission must hold hearings and report conclusions on pending legislation when requested by the legislature, either chamber, or governor, and may recommend legislation in the public interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 history note; replaced both hallucinated penalty headings to reflect public records/annual report to the governor and legislative hearings/recommendations.

headings.title: Persons and entities authorized to file complaints
headings.reviewNote: Commission, public counsel, persons, organizations, or municipalities may complain of violations of law, rule, tariff, or order; rate-reasonableness complaints require commission motion, public counsel, local officials, or 25+ consumers/prospective consumers.

headings.title: Joinder of causes and parties in hearings and review
headings.reviewNote: All complaint matters may be joined in one hearing; no motion for misjoinder or nonjoinder of causes or parties entertained before commission or on judicial review.

headings.title: Absence of direct damage and service of complaint
headings.reviewNote: Commission not required to dismiss a complaint for absence of direct damage to complainant; must serve a copy of filed complaint on party complained of.

headings.title: Method of service in commission proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Service in commission hearings, investigations, and proceedings may be made on persons eligible for civil summons, personally or by prepaid sealed mail.

headings.title: Time, place, and ten-day notice of hearing
headings.reviewNote: Commission fixes hearing time and place and serves notice at least ten days beforehand unless public necessity requires an earlier date.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-2018 history, section 393.1675 nonseverability cross-reference, and 1976 case annotations; retained subsection 1 and corrected shifted/hallucinated headings in subsections 2-5.

headings.title: Procedural rules and nonbinding technical evidence rules
headings.reviewNote: Hearings governed by commission-adopted rules; commission and commissioners not bound by technical rules of evidence in investigations, inquiries, or hearings.

headings.title: Procedural formality not invalidating commission orders
headings.reviewNote: Archived text states 'No formality' (while catchline says 'proceedings to be informal') in any proceeding or taking of testimony shall invalidate commission orders, decisions, rules, or regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939-1996 history notes; refined both headings and explicitly noted the source text's 'No formality' phrasing versus the catchline's 'proceedings to be informal'.

headings.title: Right to be heard, intervention, and witness process
headings.reviewNote: Complainant, public counsel, respondent utility, and permitted intervenors entitled to be heard and introduce evidence; commission issues process to enforce attendance of necessary witnesses.

headings.title: Written investigation reports and witness depositions
headings.reviewNote: Commission must make written report stating conclusions and decision after investigation; commission or any party may take in-state or out-of-state depositions with subpoena power and circuit-court fees.

headings.title: Additional time and extensions for order compliance
headings.reviewNote: Commission may grant additional time when order cannot be complied with in 30 days and extend compliance time for good cause shown.

headings.title: Hearing record, review stipulations, and rate reconciliations
headings.reviewNote: Requires full formal hearing record and reporter transcript (printed transcript waivable unanimously), allows stipulated review records, and requires detailed dollar/rate reconciliation and billing determinants in non-price-cap/non-competitive rate cases for section 386.520 remand relief.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-2011 history (effective 7-01-11), Chap. 536 cross-reference, and 1960 intervention annotation; replaced shifted/hallucinated headings in subsections 1-3 and expanded subsection 4 to include rate reconciliations.

headings.title: Subpoena issuance, service, and state-paid witness fees
headings.reviewNote: Commissioner or secretary signs and issues statewide subpoenas; process servers and commission-ordered witnesses receive circuit-court civil fees and mileage audited and paid by the state.

headings.title: Party-paid subpoena costs and advance fee demand
headings.reviewNote: Parties other than public counsel bear service and witness fees for their subpoenas; non-commission-paid witnesses may demand travel and one-day fee at service; no mileage if furnished free transportation.

headings.title: Free certified copies and filings from public officers
headings.reviewNote: Public officers must furnish certified copies of filed documents and enter, file, docket, or record documents for the commission or public counsel without charge.

headings.title: State payment of public counsel witness fees
headings.reviewNote: Witnesses subpoenaed at the public counsel's instance receive circuit-court civil fees and mileage audited and paid by the state upon sworn vouchers approved by the public counsel.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939/1977 history notes; replaced all 4 hallucinated deposition headings to reflect subpoena issuance/state-paid fees, party-paid costs/advance fee demands, free public-officer copies/filings, and public counsel witness fees.

headings.title: Service of commission orders and method of transmittal
headings.reviewNote: Orders served by personal delivery of certified copy, electronic service, or prepaid sealed mail to affected person or corporate officer/agent eligible for civil summons.

headings.title: Thirty-day effective date and continuing force of orders
headings.reviewNote: Orders take effect 30 days after service unless otherwise provided and continue for designated period or until changed/abrogated, unless unauthorized by law or unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939/2011 history notes; updated subsection 1 note for electronic service and replaced subsection 2 heading to remove ungrounded acknowledgment-of-receipt claim and reflect the 30-day effective date.

headings.title: Right to apply for rehearing and thirty-day decision
headings.reviewNote: Public counsel or interested party may apply for rehearing; commission grants if sufficient reason appears and must decide granted rehearings within 30 days after final submission.

headings.title: Rehearing prerequisite to court action and specific grounds
headings.reviewNote: No court action accrues unless rehearing application is made before order's effective date stating specific grounds; applicant cannot urge unlisted grounds in court.

headings.title: No automatic stay of order during rehearing application
headings.reviewNote: Rehearing application does not excuse compliance or stay/postpone enforcement of a commission order except as the commission directs.

headings.title: Modification or abrogation of orders after rehearing
headings.reviewNote: After rehearing, commission may abrogate, change, or modify original order; new order has same force as original without affecting rights arising under original order.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939/1977 history notes; fixed shifted headings across all 4 subsections covering rehearing application/30-day decision, court-review prerequisite and specific grounds, no automatic stay, and post-rehearing modification.

headings.title: No automatic stay and appellate stay for non-rate orders
headings.reviewNote: Pending section 386.510 appeal does not automatically stay order; for non-rate orders issued on/after July 1, 2011, appellate court may grant stay upon appeal bond and showing of great or irreparable damage.

headings.title: No stay for rate orders and remand rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Bars stays of non-price-cap/non-competitive rate orders issued on/after July 1, 2011; details temporary/prospective remand rate adjustments with prime-minus-two (floor zero) interest, 60/120-day remand deadlines (original rolls footnote on 'and'), and 90-day remand for inadequate findings.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-2011 history (effective 7-01-11), original-rolls footnote ('and' in 'one hundred * twenty days'), and Chap. 470 cross-reference; replaced hallucinated subsection 1 heading and broadened subsection 2 to cover the rate-order stay bar and remand procedures.

headings.title: Rehearing or transfer to Missouri Supreme Court
headings.reviewNote: Aggrieved party in court of appeals may seek rehearing or transfer to supreme court; certified PSC record serves as appeal record.

headings.title: Immediate docketing and priority hearing in Supreme Court
headings.reviewNote: Appeals to supreme court immediately placed on docket, having precedence over other civil causes of different nature.

headings.title: Application of general appellate procedural laws
headings.reviewNote: General laws relating to appellate practice apply to commission appeals so far as not in conflict with chapter.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939-2011 history (effective 7-01-11), and 1967 cost-bond annotation; all 3 headings retained covering supreme court rehearing/transfer and certified record, immediate docketing/precedence, and general appellate laws.

headings.title: General penalty for statutory or commission order violations
headings.reviewNote: Corporation, person, or public utility violating state constitution, law, or commission order/rule where no other penalty provided is subject to $100 to $2,000 penalty per offense.

headings.title: Separate offenses for continuing violations
headings.reviewNote: Every violation is separate offense; in continuing violations each day constitutes separate and distinct offense.

headings.title: Corporate liability for acts and omissions of agents
headings.reviewNote: Act, omission, or failure of officer, agent, or employee within scope of duty deemed act of corporation or utility.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 history note; all 3 headings retained covering $100-$2,000 general penalties, separate daily offenses for continuing violations, and imputation of employee/agent acts.

headings.title: Natural gas pipeline safety standards and municipal plants
headings.reviewNote: Unlawful to violate federal or state natural gas safety standards; municipal gas plants subject to safety laws and rules.

headings.title: Maximum civil penalties based on federal transportation limits
headings.reviewNote: Penalties aligned with federal 49 CFR Part 190.223(a) limits; commission considers gravity, culpability, and ability to pay.

headings.title: Separate offenses for each day of gas safety violations
headings.reviewNote: Each safety standard violation is a separate offense even within the same incident; each day of continuing violation constitutes a separate offense.

headings.title: Imputation of employee safety acts to gas plant operators
headings.reviewNote: Act or omission of employee within scope of duty considered act of corporation, utility, or municipality owning gas plant.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2008/2025 history notes; all 4 headings retained covering federally mandated natural gas safety compliance, 49 CFR Part 190.223(a) penalty caps and factors, separate/daily offenses, and employee-act imputation.

headings.title: Public counsel powers, staffing, and representation discretion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public counsel to employ staff/contract experts, represent public interests in PSC proceedings/appeals, and exercise representation discretion including conflict certification to the department of economic development director.

headings.title: Mandatory service of tariffs, pleadings, and commission orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires service on public counsel of all proposed tariffs, initial pleadings, applications, and commission orders.

headings.title: Preservation of public counsel right to appeal
headings.reviewNote: Enumerated chapter 386 sections shall not be construed to deny public counsel's right to appeal any PSC order to the courts under section 386.500.

headings.title: Necessary and proper implied powers
headings.reviewNote: Grants public counsel all powers necessary or proper to carry out the duties specified in this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1977 history note; replaced shifted/hallucinated headings across all 4 subsections to match staffing/representation discretion, mandatory service of filings and orders, preserved right of appeal, and necessary-and-proper powers.

headings.title: Annual public counsel expense estimates by utility group
headings.reviewNote: Starting FY July 1, 2026, public counsel estimates annual office expenses under sections 386.700 and 386.710 by utility group (water/sewer combined) and unallocated expenses; telephone and telegraph corporations exempt.

headings.title: Expense allocation and assessment cap on utilities
headings.reviewNote: Public counsel allocates direct and proportional unallocated expenses by group and assesses utilities proportionally based on gross intrastate revenues, capped at 0.057% of total regulated utility revenues.

headings.title: Assessment statements and payment or installment schedule
headings.reviewNote: Public counsel renders statements by July 1; utilities pay director of revenue in full by July 15 or in four equal installments (July 15, Oct 15, Jan 15, Apr 15); remitted to state treasurer.

headings.title: Office of the Public Counsel Fund and carryover reductions
headings.reviewNote: Treasurer credits payments to Office of the Public Counsel Fund (or successor under repealed section 33.571*); unexpended balances do not revert and reduce next year's assessments proportionally.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 2025 S.B. 4 history, and footnote noting repeal of section 33.571 (H.B. 1965, 2010); replaced all 4 hallucinated headings to reflect OPC fiscal expense estimates, 0.057% assessment cap, billing/installment schedule, and OPC Fund carryovers.

headings.title: Prohibition on utilities engaging in HVAC services
headings.reviewNote: Utility may not engage in HVAC services unless otherwise provided in subsection 8.

headings.title: At-cost compensation for regulated utility assets used
headings.reviewNote: Affiliate or utility contractor may not use vehicles, tools, employees, or other rate-recoverable utility assets for HVAC services unless utility is compensated at cost.

headings.title: Required disclaimer when using utility name
headings.reviewNote: Utility, affiliate, or utility contractor using utility name for HVAC services must display bold written or audible disclaimer that services are not PSC-regulated.

headings.title: Prohibition on cross-subsidizing HVAC services
headings.reviewNote: Utility may not engage in or assist HVAC services in a manner subsidizing them so as to alter regulated utility rates.

headings.title: Separate books and records for HVAC entities
headings.reviewNote: Affiliates or utility contractors engaged in HVAC services must maintain accounts, books, and records separate and distinct from the utility.

headings.title: Applicability to affiliated or commonly controlled HVAC entities
headings.reviewNote: Applies to any HVAC affiliate or utility contractor owned, controlled, or under common control with a utility providing regulated service in Missouri or any other state.

headings.title: Grandfathered utility HVAC services in pre-1993 areas
headings.reviewNote: Utility providing HVAC services five years prior to August 28, 1998 may continue same service type in areas regularly served prior to August 28, 1993, excluding later expansions.

headings.title: Exceptions for emergency, required, or tariffed services
headings.reviewNote: Does not prohibit emergency service, legally required service, or programs under existing PSC tariff, rule, or order consistent with section.

headings.title: Open qualification process for utility HVAC contractors
headings.reviewNote: Utility engaging HVAC contractors must maintain an open qualification process allowing vendor registration and bid evaluation.

headings.title: Violation investigations, intervention, and disposition copies
headings.reviewNote: PSC staff investigates reasonable inferences of sections 386.754-386.764 violations; commission may open section 386.330 case, abate, and seek penalties (386.360/386.600); informants may intervene and receive final disposition excluding privileged documents.

headings.title: Civil penalties and attorney general enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Violating utility commits civil offense subject to up to $12,500 civil penalty per violation; attorney general may enforce under statutory or constitutional powers.

headings.title: Permit compliance and waiver of grandfathered exemption
headings.reviewNote: Utility claiming subsection 7 exemption must comply with state/local HVAC laws and permit requirements; continuing noncompliance supports finding waiver of exemption.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1998-2025 history notes; replaced all 12 hallucinated affiliate-transaction headings to accurately reflect HVAC service prohibitions, asset cost recovery, disclaimers, cross-subsidy bar, separate records, pre-1993 grandfathering, exceptions, contractor qualification, investigations, $12,500 civil penalties, and exemption waiver.

headings.title: Commission administration authority and limitation on HVAC rules
headings.reviewNote: PSC has full authority to administer sections 386.754-386.764 but may not impose HVAC requirements inconsistent with or additional to those sections or section 386.315.

headings.title: Prohibition on actions allowing statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: PSC shall not adopt any rule, tariff, order, or action purporting to allow a violation of sections 386.754-386.764.

headings.title: Chapter 536 compliance for promulgated rules
headings.reviewNote: No rule or portion of a rule promulgated under sections 386.754-386.764 becomes effective unless promulgated under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1998/2025 history notes; replaced all 3 hallucinated code-of-conduct headings to match PSC administration/limits under sections 386.754-386.764, bar on permitting violations, and chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Prohibition on outside municipal electric service and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Bars municipal electric utilities from retail service outside corporate boundaries after July 11, 1991, except pre-existing service, section 394.312 agreements, annexation, or acquired utility territories (with PSC 120-day expansion procedure for qualifying first-class-county cities over 125,000).

headings.title: Annexation extensions and mandatory good-faith negotiations
headings.reviewNote: Allows municipal extension into unserved annexed areas; if rural electric cooperative has facilities within one mile, majority of landowners/developers/customers may invoke 45-day negotiations considering seven factors, after which customer preference controls (excluding municipal property).

headings.title: Commission determination when electrical corporation serves municipality
headings.reviewNote: Applies subsection 2 when an electrical corporation serves the municipality, except failed 45-day negotiations go to PSC for a 120-day public-interest order considering subsection 2(1)-(7) factors (original rolls footnote: 'through'), reviewable under 386.500-386.550.

headings.title: Notice and governing-body approval for served annexed structures
headings.reviewNote: To extend service to annexed structures served by another supplier within 90 days pre-annexation, municipal utility must publish/give written notice within 60 days and obtain governing-body approval to negotiate within six months.

headings.title: Negotiation of territorial agreements and power purchase alternatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires good-faith negotiation of territorial agreement, transfers, franchise alternative, or equivalent power purchase contract within 180 days (extendable up to 180 days by mutual agreement and written PSC request).

headings.title: Definition of fair and reasonable compensation
headings.reviewNote: Defines fair and reasonable compensation as reproduction cost new less straight-line depreciation, detachment/reintegration costs, 200% of normalized 12-month gross revenues less gross receipts taxes, transaction taxes, and other reasonable costs.

headings.title: Commission assignment of territories and compensation orders
headings.reviewNote: If subsection 5 negotiations fail, either party may apply within 60 days for PSC evidentiary hearing and 120-day order assigning exclusive territories and compensation, reviewable under 386.500-386.550, with payment and transfer within 90 days after finality.

headings.title: Factors for commission territorial and compensation decisions
headings.reviewNote: Lists four factors PSC must consider under subsection 7: public interest (including owner preference and rate disparities/discrimination), fair compensation, system operation effects, and agreed issues.

headings.title: Limited commission jurisdiction, load cap, and case fees
headings.reviewNote: Grants PSC necessary jurisdiction over municipal utilities and cooperatives for this section, bars compelling transfer of structures/customers over 1,000 kW connected load, requires case-by-case cost-recovery fee rules, and disclaims broader jurisdiction.

headings.title: Rural electric cooperative service within municipal boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Allows rural electric cooperative to serve within municipal boundaries notwithstanding 394.020/394.080 if provided under subsections 2 to 9 (original rolls footnote: 'through') and conditioned on territorial and municipal franchise agreements (which may require sales tax collection).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1991/2021 history, and original-rolls footnote ('through' in H.B. 271 and S.B. 44, 2021); replaced all 10 hallucinated headings to reflect municipal extraterritorial restrictions, annexation negotiations, PSC determinations, fair-compensation formula, 1,000 kW limit, and cooperative municipal service.

headings.title: Advanced and traditional meter opt-out definitions
headings.reviewNote: Defines advanced meter, hub meter, inaccurate information, regular basis, traditional meter, and utility (rate-regulated under chapter 386 or 393; original-rolls footnote notes 'chapters').

headings.title: Residential meter opt-out process, fees, and self-reading
headings.reviewNote: Requires PSC opt-out rules by June 30, 2026; allows residential opt-out starting July 1, 2026 with max $125 one-time and $15 monthly fees, sets self-reading/annual verification/interest (max 5%) rules, and limits utility liability for customer-reading injuries absent willful misconduct or gross negligence.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs PSC to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028; nonseverable with legislative rule-review powers (rules after Aug 28, 2025 void if review powers held unconstitutional).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 2025 S.B. 4 history, and original-rolls footnote ('chapters'); replaced all 3 hallucinated EV-charging headings to reflect advanced/hub meter opt-out definitions, residential opt-out/fees/self-reading rules, and chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Task force establishment and membership
headings.reviewNote: Establishes Task Force on Distributed Energy Resources and Net Metering with legislative, agency (division of energy, PSC, OPC), electric industry, distributed energy, renewable advocacy, and low-income advocacy members.

headings.title: Public hearings, research, and legislative report
headings.reviewNote: Directs task force to hold public hearings, conduct research, and deliver report to general assembly by December 31, 2023 covering distributed energy/value-of-solar study, community solar/rate equity, and net metering changes.

headings.title: Initial meeting, officers, and quorum requirements
headings.reviewNote: Task force must meet within 30 days of creation, select legislative chair and vice chair from opposite chambers, meet as necessary, and act by majority vote of a majority quorum.

headings.title: Legislative research staff support
headings.reviewNote: House research and senate research staff provide requested clerical, research, fiscal, and legal services.

headings.title: Division of energy study oversight and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Division of energy oversees independent expert study funded by federal/state grants and establishes procedures for confidential and proprietary information.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Task force members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual and necessary official expenses.

headings.title: Contingent expiration date of section
headings.reviewNote: Section expires December 31, 2023, or upon conclusion of task force work, whichever is sooner (source footnote notes contingent expiration date).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 2022 history, and contingent-expiration footnote; replaced all 7 hallucinated gas-surcharge headings to reflect the Task Force on Distributed Energy Resources and Net Metering, its 2023 report, organization, staff support, study oversight, reimbursement, and contingent expiration.

headings.title: Short title of Net Metering and Easy Connection Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section as the 'Net Metering and Easy Connection Act'.

headings.title: Net metering definitions
headings.reviewNote: Defines avoided fuel cost, commission, customer-generator (up to 100 kW renewable), department, net metering, renewable energy resources, and retail electric supplier (including cooperative-plan electrical corporations under 393.110(2)).

headings.title: Retail electric supplier availability, tariff, and disclosure duties
headings.reviewNote: Suppliers must offer first-come net metering up to 5% single-hour peak load (1% annual cap), offer identical base tariffs without extra standby/interconnection fees, and make annual program disclosures.

headings.title: Metering equipment and customer reimbursement of costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires net metering equipment; customer-generator reimburses supplier for needed additional meter/distribution equipment (optionally amortized over up to 12 billing cycles with reasonable interest) and subsequent customer-necessitated meter changes.

headings.title: Net electrical energy measurement, billing, and credit expiration
headings.reviewNote: Specifies bidirectional or multiple metering, net billing, excess generation credits at avoided fuel cost expiring after 12 months or termination without compensation, and optional wholesale-generator credits for co-ops/municipals.

headings.title: Safety standards, disconnect switch, and small-system exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires code/IEEE/UL compliance; bars unauthorized fees while allowing manual external disconnect switch; exempts <=10 kW systems from extra controls/tests/insurance and directs rules/exemptions for >10 kW systems.

headings.title: Interconnection applications, review deadlines, and ownership changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires wiring plan/specs, 30-day (<=10 kW) or 90-day (>10 kW) supplier review, electrician/engineer certification, one-year approval expiration, and new application upon ownership change.

headings.title: Annual net metering reports by retail electric suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Electrical corporations report annually to PSC (other suppliers to governing body and consumers on request) on customer-generator count, capacity, and net kilowatt-hours received.

headings.title: Commission rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs PSC to adopt initial rules within 9 months of Jan 1, 2008 including simple contracts and all-in-one <=10 kW applications; subject to chapter 536/536.028 nonseverability (rules after Aug 28, 2007 void if review powers invalid).

headings.title: Cooperative and municipal utility simple contract policies
headings.reviewNote: Cooperative and municipal governing bodies must adopt simple contract policies and all-in-one <=10 kW application documents within 9 months of January 1, 2008.

headings.title: Retail electric supplier liability standard
headings.reviewNote: Retail electric supplier has no liability for property or personal damages caused by customer-generator unit or interconnection absent clear and convincing evidence of supplier fault.

headings.title: Credit toward renewable energy portfolio targets
headings.reviewNote: Estimated generating capacity of net metering systems counts toward retail electric supplier's state renewable energy portfolio targets or mandates.

headings.title: Consumer protection, disclosure rules, and attorney general enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Subjects generation unit sales to sections 407.010-407.145 and 407.700-407.720; authorizes attorney general chapter 536 disclosure rules and investigation/enforcement of misrepresentation or safety dangers.

headings.title: Rate recovery of supplier net metering costs
headings.reviewNote: Retail electric supplier costs incurred under 'this act' (2007/2022 disposition-table footnote) are recoverable in the utility's rate structure.

headings.title: Prohibition on unapproved parallel connection and disconnection
headings.reviewNote: Bars parallel connection without written supplier approval under subsection 7(1); allows immediate disconnection and service termination without notice for violation.

headings.title: Manufacturer liability for defective generation units
headings.reviewNote: Manufacturer of a qualified generation unit may be held liable for property or personal damages caused by a defect in the unit.

headings.title: Liability for knowing safety misrepresentation
headings.reviewNote: Seller, installer, or manufacturer knowingly misrepresenting safety aspects of a qualified generation unit may be held liable for resulting property or personal damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 2007-2022 history, and 'this act' disposition-table footnote; replaced all 17 shifted/hallucinated headings across the Net Metering and Easy Connection Act.

headings.title: Renewable natural gas program definitions
headings.reviewNote: Defines biogas, biomass, gas corporation, qualified investment, renewable natural gas, and RNG infrastructure.

headings.title: Commission rules for voluntary renewable natural gas program
headings.reviewNote: Commission adopts rules for gas corporations to offer voluntary RNG program, reporting, and prudent cost recovery once operational and producing RNG for customer use.

headings.title: Required contents of gas corporation program filing
headings.reviewNote: Filing must include proposed procurement volume over specified period and identification of qualified infrastructure investments.

headings.title: Annual revision limit on program filings
headings.reviewNote: Gas corporation may revise program filing submitted to commission no more than one time per year.

headings.title: Rate recovery through automatic rate adjustment clause
headings.reviewNote: Prudent and reasonable costs incurred for qualified investments may be recovered through automatic rate adjustment clause.

headings.title: Inclusion of general rate case cost of capital
headings.reviewNote: Costs of qualified production investments include cost of capital established in most recent general rate case.

headings.title: Division of energy report on program benefits and metrics
headings.reviewNote: Division of energy reports to legislative leaders by January 1, 2023, on project counts, volumes, emissions, and economic impacts.

headings.title: Affiliate investment in biogas production facilities
headings.reviewNote: Rules cannot prohibit gas corporation affiliate from investing in biogas production if affiliate is not a public utility.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Commission may promulgate rules under chapter 536; rules nonseverable if legislative review powers held invalid.

headings.title: Nine-year sunset provision and continuing rate adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Section expires nine years from program establishment under section 23.253 sunset act (source footnote); authorized rate adjustments continue while program remains operational and produces RNG.
